Writes the text at $88/$89 out in full into message_buffer, with every '@' part copied in, ends it with '$' and points $88/$89 at radio_header, the text the radio shows.
Copies a text to the place at $80/$81 up to its '$', going into each '@' part.
The radio message's frame: "RYRYRY...", the letters R and Y nineteen times (the test line of a teleprinter), and a carriage return; the expanded message follows it in message_buffer.
200 bytes where expand_text writes the intercepted message, ended by '$'.
A second "RYRY..." line, a carriage return and "$" after the buffer, to $AD14. expand_text ends the message with its own '$', so the line is never printed.
$88/$89 becomes the word at entry A of the table at $88/$89: the step every text and script table lookup goes through.
Picks a random country that still exists as country A ($8A), and sets up its record ($8E/$8F), its relationship row ($9E/$9F) and its event levels ($96/$97).

Sets up the two countries of an event, A in $8A and B in $8B: their records ($8E, $90), relationship rows ($9E, $A0) and event levels ($96, $98), and their names as the texts at $5B34 (A) and $5B3C (B). A number of 16 or more halts the game with the border showing it (halt_with_border): a check left from testing. Then sets up C and D, each country's best friend (set_country_c, set_country_d).
Scratch for country_reply: the country that answers.
An event level of 0 matches a hostility of 0 or 1.
An event level of $FF matches a hostility of $FE or $FF.

The other side's turn after an event: the two countries swap, and if both still exist the one that was the target looks in its own event levels for one within one of its hostility to the first, and runs it. A level of 0 matches a hostility of 0 or 1 (level_zero), and the level $FF only $FE or $FF (level_ff). When none fits the exchange ends ($5B45 = 0).

Once each tick of the game clock: if an exchange is going on, the reply (country_reply). Otherwise picks a random country A and goes through the others, from a random one, for a country B such that one of A's event levels lies within one of A's hostility to B; runs the first such event between them and marks an exchange as going on. The difference is taken as a signed byte and a level of 0 is passed over, but $FF is not treated apart as country_reply treats it: $FF less a hostility of 0 is -1, so a country whose hostility to another has fallen to 0 matches event 0 first and launches a Total Missile Attack on it. When A has no event for anyone, it grows more hostile to every country by one (relations_row_up).

When no intercept was found, and country A transmits on the band the radio is on: while the radio scans, or by a 1 in 256 chance when it is stopped, A reports its relationship with a random other country B, "Our relationship with B is" a word from relation_words for A's hostility to B (divided by 32), shown scrambled on the radio (radio_message).

Every fourth tick: tries for a radio intercept (intercept_pick). When there is one, the message it picks (0 to 7) from intercept_texts is shown scrambled on the radio (radio_message) and its script, from intercept_scripts, is run (each is only an end).
Picks two different random countries as A and B and sets them up. Never called.

When no Big Bird message was found: counts the satellites' cover (satellite_census), and from a random country on finds one under exactly one Big Bird that still exists as country A, and a random other country B. Shows the satellite heading and "Their opinion of the above country is" a word from relation_words for A's hostility to B (divided by 32), in a window until fire. The heading names Big Bird bigbird_number, which only bigbird_over_a sets, so it is the number from the last Big Bird message, or 0 before the first.
open_window's inline bytes for the opinion report: column 2, row 2, 20 by 15 cells, colour $5D.
Picks the word for A's hostility to B, writes its address into the opinion text and prints it in the window, then waits for fire and closes it.

Every fourth tick, one after radio_intercept: tries for a Big Bird report (bigbird_pick); without one it reports an opinion instead (bigbird_none). With one, when country A is under one of the Big Birds (bigbird_over_a) it shows "BIG BIRD MESSAGE" with the message from bigbird_texts and runs its script from bigbird_scripts (each only an end).
open_window's inline bytes for the Big Bird message: column 1, row 1, 20 by 15 cells, colour $16.
Prints "BIG BIRD MESSAGE" after `jsr print_inline`.
The text "BIG BIRD MESSAGE", a carriage return and '$', after `jsr print_inline`.
Prints the Big Bird message from bigbird_texts, waits for fire and closes the window, then runs the message's script.

Is country A under one of the three Big Birds in orbit (in_cover)? Sets bigbird_number to its number, 1 to 3, and clears the condition flag; with none, bigbird_number is 0 and the flag is set. Also script command $36.
The Big Bird over country A, 1 to 3, or 0 for none.

Picks a random country A and looks through B = 0 to 15 for one whose hostility from A lies within 9 of one of A's eight bigbird_levels; returns with the carry clear and the level's number in $85, or the carry set when there is none.

Up to seven tries to find a random country A on the radio's band; then, on half the tries left by a random bit, looks through the countries B for a hostility within 9 of one of A's intercept_levels. Returns as bigbird_pick does.
The number of the event or script being run.

Runs event X between countries A and B: keeps them as the last pair ($5B46, $5B47), sets them up and works out from their missile power whether a demand comes first (demand_check). For events other than 0 and 1, a demand comes first when it is due (demand). Then looks up the event's script in event_scripts and runs it with the script engine.
Runs entry event_number of event_scripts: sets the script's address as the engine's pointer and goes into the engine's loop.

The script engine: reads the next command byte, moves the pointer on, takes the command's routine from script_commands and jumps to it with the loop's own address as its return, so each command's `rts` comes back here for the next.
The `jmp` whose operand script_loop writes with the command's routine.
The low byte of the command's routine.
The high byte of the command's routine.
Script command $15, end: drops the loop's return, so the engine returns to whoever started it.
Runs entry A of the script table at $88/$89 with the engine.

A demand from country A on country B before an event. If A has less than 11 of natural resources and B has some, "The Above country has demanded 10 U.N units of Food."; failing that, the same for technology ("of Tech."); each with Ignore, Yes and No. Yes gives one unit of the demand from B to A and the event does not happen; No lets the event go ahead; Ignore makes it worse: the two countries' hostility is set to the level of the next harsher event, and that event runs instead (demand_ignored).
Yes to a food demand: one unit of natural resources from B to A, unless A already has 15 or B has none.
Ignore: unless the event is already event 0, sets A's hostility to B and B's to A to the levels of the event one harsher, and runs that event instead.
Goes on to the event's script.
The technology demand, made when the food one is not: A has less than 11 technology and B has some.
The food demand's text: the demand heading (text_demand) and "10 U.N units of Food.", and the request for advice after it.
The technology demand's text: the heading and "10 U.N units of Tech.", and the request for advice.
The heading of a demand: country A's name, then "The Above country has demanded".
"Please Advise." and country B's name, the end of a demand.
Shows the text at $88/$89 in a window and the Ignore, Yes and No menu below it; returns the row chosen, 0 Ignore, 1 Yes, 2 No.
open_window's inline bytes for a demand: column 1, row 1, 20 by 15 cells, colour $16.
Prints the demand's text (passed on the stack) and opens the menu below it.
open_window's inline bytes for the demand's menu: column 5, row 18, 10 by 3 cells, colour $2F, flags 3, a menu (list 2, Ignore, Yes and No).
Waits for fire on Ignore, Yes or No, keeps the row, turns the cursor off and closes the menu and the demand.
After 52 weeks: works out the rating, (16 less the countries destroyed) × 48 / 4, and shows "Your year as Supreme Commander is over. Your rating is" and the number (game_over with message 2).
The rating the end of the year shows.
Script command $20 n: ends the game with message n (game_over).
Shows game-over message $84 from game_over_texts in a letter window, waits four frames and for fire, and starts again at $7CBB, a new game.
The four game-over messages: 0 recalled for lack of confidence, 1 Armageddon, 2 the year is over, 3 recalled for incompetence.
Game-over message 0 (recalled for lack of confidence): "[text_recalled] lack of / confidence.", ended by "$".
The text "[text_communique_head] You are recalled to earth / immediately. / Due to your", ended by "$".
Game-over message 1 (Armageddon): "[text_communique_head]All life on Earth has / been extinguished by / massive radiation. / ARMAGEDDON.....", ended by "$".
Game-over message 2 (the year is over): "[text_communique_head] / Your year as / Supreme Commander is / over. / Your rating is [the number at $B401]", ended by "$".
Game-over message 3 (recalled for incompetence): "[text_recalled] / incompetence.", ended by "$".
Script command $4C n: B and the country B is most hostile to (most_hostile) grow more hostile to each other by n, each byte stopping at 255.
Scratch for script_enemy_a and script_enemy_b: the enemy found.
Script command $30 n: A and the country A is most hostile to grow more hostile to each other by n, each byte stopping at 255.
Scratch: the country whose enemy was found.
Script command $0D, two bytes: the address of a table of script addresses; goes to the entry for the menu row last chosen (menu_answer).
The menu row chosen in the last script menu (script_menu), 0 for the first.
The script engine's pointer to the next byte, low byte; high byte at $B5E5.
The high byte of the script pointer.
Script command $19: waits for fire to be let go and pressed, and closes the top window.
Script command $18: prints the text of the event being run (event_texts, entry event_number) in the top window and waits 20 frames or for fire.
Script command $14 n: prints event text n in the top window.
Script command $12 w h: opens a memo's window, w by h cells at column 1, row 1, colour $63, starts its text on row 4 and draws the word MEMO (picture 8) at its top left.
open_window's inline bytes: column 1, row 1, the width and height written from the command's bytes, colour $63.
The window's width, written by script_window.
The window's height, written by script_window.
Starts the window's text on row 4 and draws picture 8 at its column and row.

Script command $11 w h n: opens a menu window w by h cells at column 20, row 5, colour $2F, with list n (menu_lists); waits for fire, keeps the row the cursor is on in menu_answer and closes the menu. A table for script_switch needs an entry for each row of the window.
open_window's inline bytes for the menu: column 20, row 5, the size written from the command, colour $2F, and the flags byte written with the list number times 2 plus 1.
The menu window's width, written by script_menu.
The menu window's height, written by script_menu.
The menu window's flags: the list number times 2, plus 1 for a menu.
Waits for fire, keeps the cursor's row (window byte 11) in menu_answer, turns the cursor off and closes the menu.
Points $80/$81 at C's hostility to D.
Points $80/$81 at D's hostility to A.
Points $80/$81 at B's hostility to A.
Points $80/$81 at A's hostility to B: A's row of the relationship table plus B.
Script command $05 n: B's hostility to A goes up by n, stopping at 255.
Script command $2E n: C's hostility to D goes up by n.
Script command $2D n: D's hostility to A goes up by n.
Script command $04 n: A's hostility to B goes up by n.
Takes the next byte of the script into $84 and moves the pointer on.
Script command $09: B's hostility to A goes up by 1 or 2, at random.
Script command $08: A's hostility to B goes up by 1 or 2.
Adds $84 to the hostility byte at $80/$81, stopping at 255.
Script command $07 n: B's hostility to A goes down by n, stopping at 0.
C's hostility to D down by n, as script_b_to_a_down does: no command in script_commands leads here.
D's hostility to A down by n; no command leads here either.
Script command $06 n: A's hostility to B goes down by n, stopping at 0.
Takes $84 from the hostility byte at $80/$81, stopping at 0.
Script command $0B: B's hostility to A goes down by 1 to 4, at random.
Script command $0A: A's hostility to B goes down by 1 to 4.
Script command $37: B's confidence in you goes down by the mail's amount (mail_amount), stopping at 0.
Script command $38: A's confidence goes down by the mail's amount.
Script command $29 n: C's confidence in you goes down by n.
Script command $2A n: D's confidence goes down by n.
Script command $03 n: B's confidence goes down by n.
Script command $02 n: A's confidence goes down by n.
Takes $84 from byte 9, the confidence in you, of the record at $80/$81, stopping at 0.
Script command $39: B's confidence goes up by the mail's amount, stopping at 255.
Script command $3A: A's confidence goes up by the mail's amount.
Script command $2B n: C's confidence goes up by n.
Script command $2C n: D's confidence goes up by n.
Script command $01 n: B's confidence goes up by n.
Script command $00 n: A's confidence goes up by n.
Adds $84 to the confidence byte of the record at $80/$81, stopping at 255.
Script command $0F: rolls against B's confidence in you: the flag is set when a random byte is at or above it, so it stays clear more often the more B trusts you.
Script command $0E: rolls against A's confidence in you, as script_roll_b does.
Script command $2F n: sets the flag when a random byte is n or more.
Clears the flag, then sets it when a random byte is at or above $84; returns with the carry from that comparison.
Clears the script's condition flag. Also script command $34.
Sets the condition flag. Also script command $33.
The scripts' condition flag, 0 or 1.
Script command $10: when the flag is set, skips the next three bytes of the script, which the scripts always fill with a `go to` (command $0C): so the jump is taken when the flag is clear.

Script command $49: sets the flag when A's missile power, as demand_check last worked it out, is not 0; it adds the two bytes rather than testing each, so a power of 511, 766, 1021 or 1276 reads as none.

Works out from the two countries' missile power (missile_power) whether a demand comes before the event: none when B has no power or A's is less than B's; otherwise demand_due is set when a random byte falls below 255 divided by A's power over B's, so it is likelier the closer the two are.
The missile power of the country whose record is at $80/$81: 3 × MX1 + 2 × MX2 + MX3, in $88/$89.
Script command $17, two bytes: calls the script at that address; script_return comes back after the command. There is one return address, so a called script cannot call another.
Script command $16: goes back to the script after the last script_call.
Where script_return goes back to, low byte; high byte at $B9DA.
The high byte of the return address.
Script command $0C, two bytes: goes on at that address.
Divides $88/$89 by $86/$87 with divide16, the quotient in $88/$89, keeping $86/$87.
Empties the four mail slots: for each, from the last, copies its start address into its next-entry address and sets its count to 0.
Ends the game with message 1, Armageddon (game_over).
Ends the year (year_over).

The end of a week, every eighth tick of the clock and at the start of a game. Mail still in this week's slot went unread: each entry is taken (in_tray_next) and, with week_ending set, runs its follow-up instead of being shown. Then the slot moves on one, the week goes up by one, the force comes a week nearer (force_weeks), and every country grows more hostile to every other by one (relations_all_up). From $BAE9 (also after a RAMLOAD): radiation of 255 ends the game with Armageddon, week 52 ends the year; otherwise the communique: the rating, from the sum of the 16 countries' confidence in you divided by 512 (0 to 7, text_rating_disastrous to text_rating_excellent), with the radiation word (radiation divided by 32, or "Background." at 0), in the letter window, then its menu (communique_menu).
The text "Background.", ended by "$": the radiation word when there is no radiation at all.

Script command $13 n w x: posts mail n, from the event's countries A and B, into the slot w weeks ahead (week_slot plus w, of the four), as three bytes: n, A × 16 + B, and x, the mail's amount. With n = $FF it posts follow-up x instead. A slot that holds 20 entries takes no more.
The slot is empty: "No Mail in Mail Box." (no_mail).

Takes the newest entry from this week's mail slot: the mail's number into mail_number, its countries into A ($8A) and B ($8B), its amount into mail_amount, and delivers it (mail_deliver). With the slot empty it says "No Mail in Mail Box.".
Script command $21 n: every country's confidence in you goes up by n, stopping at 255.
Script command $22 n: every country's confidence in you goes down by n, stopping at 0.
Country B's missiles down by 10 of each type, as script_a_missiles_down does for A: no command leads here.
Script command $1F: A's MX1, MX2 and MX3 go down by 10 each, stopping at 0.
A less 10, stopping at 0.
Script command $28: B's technology goes up by one, to 14 at most; at 14 or more the flag is set and it stays as it is.
Script command $3B: A's technology up by one, as script_b_tech_up.
Script command $3C: B's technology goes down by one; at 0 the flag is set instead.
Script command $26: A's technology down by one.
Script command $3E: B's natural resources go down by one; at 0 the flag is set instead.
Script command $25: A's natural resources down by one.
Script command $27: B's natural resources go up by one, to 14 at most, and the flag is set when they do: the opposite of the technology commands, which set it when they cannot.
Script command $3D: A's natural resources up by one, as script_b_res_up.
Script command $1E: B's MX1, MX2 and MX3 go up by 10 each, stopping at 200.
Script command $1D: A's missiles up by 10 of each type.
Script command $24: clears the flag when the U.N.N. Force is stationed in country B, and sets it otherwise.
Script command $23: clears the flag when the force is stationed in country A.
A plus 10, stopping at 200.

Delivers the entry just taken: a follow-up (mail_number $FF) runs at once (followup_run); at the end of the week, unread mail runs its follow-up (mail_unread); otherwise the mail's script runs from mail_scripts ($9C24), with A and B set up.
Script command $48: opens the letter window (column 1, row 2, 17 by 15), draws picture 9 seven columns in, and prints the mail's text from mail_texts ($9C46), then waits 20 frames or for fire.
open_window's inline bytes: column 1, row 2, 17 by 15 cells, colour $16.
Starts the text on row 4, draws picture 9, sets up the countries and prints the mail's text.
Mail left unread at the end of the week runs its follow-up script, entry mail_number of followup_scripts ($9E5F).

A follow-up entry: runs entry mail_amount of followup_scripts, then takes the next entry of the slot at once. At the week's end this takes an entry more than week_end counted, so when it was the last, the next call finds the slot empty and shows "No Mail in Mail Box.".

Counts which countries each kind of satellite covers: clears the counts (fill), then for each country counts the Big Birds over it into bigbird_cover, with their total in bigbird_total, and the SDI satellites into sdi_cover and sdi_total.
fill's inline bytes: $22 bytes (34) of 0 from $BEFF.
The two loops of satellite_census: in_bigbird_cover then in_sdi_cover for each country's record.
For each country, how many Big Birds cover it, then at $BF0F the number of countries covered.
How many countries a Big Bird covers.
For each country, how many SDI satellites cover it.
How many countries an SDI satellite covers.

The eye in the satellite panel: counts the cover (satellite_census); when an SDI satellite covers any country, lists them under "SATELLITE DEFENCE COVER" in a window as tall as the list; then the same for the Big Birds under "RECONNAISSANCE COVER". With no Big Bird cover it says "No Foot prints!" instead, whatever the SDI satellites cover.
open_window's inline bytes: column 10, row 1, 18 cells wide, as tall as the count written at $BF35, colour $16.
The window's height, the number of countries plus one.
Prints the heading and the countries the SDI satellites cover (cover_list).
The heading "SATELLITE DEFENCE COVER", ended by "$", after `jsr print_inline`.
Lists the countries in sdi_cover (cover_list); then the reconnaissance cover.
open_window's inline bytes for the reconnaissance list, as at $BF32.
The second window's height.
Prints "RECONNAISSANCE COVER" and the countries the Big Birds cover.
The heading "RECONNAISSANCE COVER", ended by "$".
Lists the countries in bigbird_cover.
"No Foot prints!" in a window at column 1, row 1, 10 by 1, until fire.
open_window's inline bytes: column 1, row 1, 10 by 1 cells, colour $72.
Prints "No Foot prints!" (after `jsr print_inline`), and waits for fire to close it.
The text "No Foot prints!", ended by "$".
Waits for fire after a do_nothing and closes the window.
Prints the name of each country whose count in the list at $86/$87 is not 0, one a line (cover_name), waits for fire and closes the window.
Prints the name of country A from cover_names, and a carriage return.
The 16 countries' names' addresses in country_names.
Is the country whose record is at $80/$81 under one of the six SDI satellites in orbit? Returns with the carry set when it is.
The same for the three Big Birds.

Is the thing at $80/$81 (a country's record, or a missile) under the satellite at $82/$83? The satellite's x must lie from the thing's x less 4 (less the satellite's reach, its byte 2, plus one) to the thing's x plus its width plus 5, and its y the same way, compared as signed bytes. Returns with the carry set when it is.
Is the cursor within 4 pixels of the satellite at $82/$83 (from 4 left of it to 3 right, and the same up and down)? Returns with the carry set when it is.

When fire is pressed on the map near a satellite in orbit (near_cursor), picks it up: the cursor takes the satellite's shape and the satellite leaves the map; it is put down where fire is next pressed inside the map ($C39F), and drawn there.
Carries the satellite found: until fire is pressed inside the map, moves the cursor; then stores the cursor's x and y as the satellite's, draws it and gives the cursor back its arrow.

Sets up a straight line for the missile at $80/$81 from x $86, y $87 to x $84, y $85: the steps in x and y (+1 or -1) for a straight move in bytes 8 and 9 and for a diagonal one in 10 and 11, the shorter distance in byte 12, the longer in byte 13, and half the longer as the running count in byte 7.
When x is the longer way, or both distances are 0, which returns at once.

Moves the missile at $80/$81 one pixel along its line: adds the shorter distance to the running count (byte 7); when it reaches the longer distance it takes it off and moves diagonally, otherwise straight. Returns the new x and y in $84 and $85.
The straight step.
Draws the satellite at $80/$81 with the cursor off: on the map it appears, or, drawn again, disappears.
Flips the 8 by 8 shape of a satellite, satellite_shape at $C2CF, into the bitmap at the x, y in bytes 0 and 1 of the record at $80/$81.
Flips the 8 by 8 shape at $86/$87 into the bitmap at the x, y of the thing at $80/$81, each row shifted across two cells by the x within its byte: drawn twice it is gone.
Scratch: the x within its byte, how far each row of the shape is shifted.
A satellite on the map: two pixels by two in the top left of an 8 by 8 shape, then six empty rows.
Copies 8 bytes from $86/$87 to $88/$89: one cell of a picture.
1 while the satellite panel is open: move_cursor then moves the cursor two pixels left or right a frame instead of three.

The satellites, from the main screen: opens the satellite panel (column 1, row 1, 7 by 10), colours its SDI and Big Bird rows, draws the eye (picture 6) and the exit (picture 4) and the nine satellites' boxes (satellite_icons). Then, until the exit is chosen: when fire is pressed on one of the panel's eleven places (panel_rects) it goes to its routine through panel_routines; elsewhere it looks for a satellite on the map to move (satellite_grab).
open_window's inline bytes for the panel: column 1, row 1, 7 by 10 cells, colour $E0.
Colours the SDI rows of the panel (fill_cells).
fill_cells' inline bytes for the SDI rows: column 1, row 1, 7 by 4, colour $A0.
Colours the Big Bird rows.
fill_cells' inline bytes for the Big Bird rows: column 1, row 5, 7 by 2, colour $B0.
Draws picture 6, the eye, at (2, 8) and picture 4, the exit, at (5, 8), puts the cursor in the panel and draws the nine satellites' places (satellite_icons); then the panel's loop.
A lone `rts` after the jump to on_goto that nothing reaches.
Fire was not on the panel: look for a satellite on the map to pick up (satellite_grab), and wait again.

The satellite panel's eleven places as hit_test rectangles (column, row, width, height and two bytes for the cursor), numbered from the last: the exit at (5, 8), the eye at (2, 8), the Big Birds 3, 2 and 1 at (6, 6), (4, 6) and (2, 6), the SDI satellites 6 to 1 at (6, 4), (4, 4), (2, 4), (6, 2), (4, 2) and (2, 2).
The map as a rectangle: column 10, row 1, 21 by 14 cells. A satellite can be put in orbit only inside it.
The panel as a rectangle: column 1, row 1, 7 by 10. Fire inside it while a satellite is carried puts it back.
The routines of the panel's places, by hit_test's number: SDI satellites 1 to 6 ($C4C7 to $C4FE), Big Birds 1 to 3 ($C4A6 to $C4BC), the eye (cover_report_icon) and the exit (info_close).
The panel's picture of an SDI satellite waiting to be placed, one cell.
The picture of a Big Bird waiting to be placed.
An empty box: the place of a satellite that is in orbit.
Draws the panel's nine places: each satellite's picture while it waits, or the empty box once it is in orbit (bigbird_icons, then sdi_icons for SDI 1 to 3 on row 2 and 4 to 6 on row 4).
Draws three SDI places from the record at $80/$81, two cells apart.
Draws the three Big Bird places on row 6.
The record of the satellite chosen on the panel, low byte; high byte at $C4A5.
The chosen satellite record's high byte.
Big Bird 1 ($5D8C) chosen on the panel.
Big Bird 2 ($5D94).
Big Bird 3 ($5D9C).
SDI satellite 1 ($5D5C).
SDI satellite 2 ($5D64).
SDI satellite 3 ($5D6C).
SDI satellite 4 ($5D74).
SDI satellite 5 ($5D7C).
SDI satellite 6 ($5D84).

A satellite chosen on the panel. One in orbit comes down: it leaves the map and its box shows its picture again. One waiting is picked up: the cursor takes the satellite shape until fire is pressed inside the map, where it goes into orbit at the cursor (bit 0 of byte 6 set, x and y from the cursor), or inside the panel, which puts it back.
The eye: the cover report (cover_report) with the cursor off.
Cleared by icon_satellites and read by nothing.
Country B's record during a war, low byte; high byte at $C5C4.
The high byte of B's record during a war.
Country A's record, low byte; high byte at $C5C6.
The high byte of A's record during a war.
The missiles A fires in the war, MX1, MX2 and MX3, then at $C5CA those B fires; each comes down by one as one of its missiles lands or is shot down.
B's missiles in the war, MX1 to MX3.

The six missiles of a war, 19 bytes each: three from $C5CD carry A's missiles to B, three from $C606 B's to A. Bytes 0 and 1 its x and y, 2 and 3 its size for in_cover (2 by 2), 6 its target country times 2 with bit 0 set while it flies, 7 to 13 its line (line_setup), 14 its type (0 MX1 to 2 MX3), 15 and 16 the routine it runs each frame, 17 and 18 the point it flies to.
The three missiles that carry B's missiles to A.
Two bytes after the six missiles that nothing reads.
Script command $1C: a limited strike. When B still exists, A fires three missiles at it, MX1 first (take_missiles), and the war runs (war_run); B does not fire back.
Takes A missiles from the record at $80/$81 into the three counts at $82/$83: MX1 first, then MX2, then MX3, as many of each as there are. Returns how many it could not find.
Returns when the target is gone.

Script command $1B: a missile exchange. When B still exists, A fires as many missiles as B can still take (its byte 10 less byte 11); then, when A still exists, B fires back as many as A can take; and the war runs.

The war on the map. Sets the interrupt's hook to nothing, clears the shoot-down count and sets up the six missiles (war_missiles_init). Every frame each missile runs its routine (war_frame), until every missile fired has landed or been shot down; then, with war_ending set, until none is still flying. Ends with the aftermath (war_report), a do_nothing and the missile report with both countries marked.
0 while the war is being fought, 1 while the last missiles finish: then a missile that lands does not go back to its launcher.
Waits a frame (wait_frames), then runs the routine of each of the six missiles (missile_run).
Jumps to the routine in bytes 15 and 16 of the missile at $80/$81, by writing it into the `jmp` at $C827.
The `jmp` whose operand missile_run writes: the missile's routine.
The low byte of the missile's routine.
The high byte of the missile's routine.

A missile in flight, each frame: when it has reached the point it flies to it explodes (missile_arrived); otherwise it moves one pixel along its line, redrawn as a dot, and may be shot down (sdi_check).
Is the missile at the point it flies to? Returns with Z set when it is.
The missile has arrived: its routine becomes missile_explode.

Launches a missile: the point it flies to is a random point in the target country's box (the record at $82/$83), and it starts from a random point in the launching country's box (missile_from); then it is drawn as a dot, its line is set up (line_setup), it is marked as flying and its routine becomes missile_fly.
The launching country's record for missile_launch, low and high byte.
The launching country's record, high byte.
The launcher of B's missiles at A, each frame while the missile waits: launches the next of B's missiles (war_b_fired), MX1 first, when any is left.

The launcher of A's missiles at B: launches the next of A's missiles (war_a_fired). The counts come down only as missiles land, so while fewer than three are left, the three launchers each launch one: a single missile fired can fly as three.
Picks the type to launch: the first of MX1, MX2 and MX3 whose count is not 0, kept in byte 14, and launches it (missile_launch); with none left the missile waits.
Takes three times the missile's type from war_tally_count, stopping at 0. Nothing reads the count.
A count that war_tally lowers and nothing reads or sets.
Sets up the six missiles: the three at $C5CD launch A's missiles at B (routine launcher_a, target B), the three at $C606 B's at A (launcher_b, target A); each is 2 by 2 for in_cover and not flying.
The missile explodes where it landed: war_tally, the dot erased, the position moved 3 up and left to centre the explosion, and the small ring (blast_small) drawn; its routine becomes blast_2.
The explosion's second frame: the small ring off, the middle ring on.
Third: the middle ring off, the large ring on.
Fourth: the large ring off, the middle ring on.
Fifth: the middle ring off, the small ring on.
The small ring off; the target takes the hit (war_damage).

A missile that has landed or been shot down: its type's count in war_a_fired or war_b_fired comes down by one, it stops flying, and it goes back to its launcher, or, with war_ending set, to missile_idle.
A missile with nothing more to do: its routine is set to itself.
Back to launcher_a, for a missile whose target was B.

For each of the six SDI satellites in orbit, by a 1 in 4 chance each, is the missile under it (in_cover)? When one is, the missile keeps the satellite in bytes 7 and 13 and its routine becomes laser_on.
An SDI satellite has the missile.
The missile's dot goes, and a laser line is drawn from the satellite to it (laser_line); its routine becomes laser_off.
The laser line is drawn again, which takes it off, the missile is counted as shot down (shot_down) and finishes as one that landed without its hit (missile_done).
How many missiles the SDI satellites shot down in the war, low byte; high at $CC0F. Cleared by war_run, counted by laser_off, never shown.
The shoot-down count's high byte.

The target, A or B, takes a hit: byte 11 goes up by one, and when it reaches byte 10 the country is destroyed: byte 11 becomes $FF, countries_destroyed goes up and its natural resources and technology become 0. A hit on a country still standing raises the radiation by one, by a 1 in 4 chance (radiation_up).
Two bytes between war_damage and radiation_up that nothing reads.
By a 1 in 4 chance, the world's radiation goes up by one, stopping at 255.
Draws the laser line between the satellite and the missile, by flipping a dot (missile_dot) at every pixel along a line set up in the scratch missile at laser_scratch.
A scratch missile for laser_line: its x and y walk from the satellite's position to the missile's.
The explosion's small ring, an 8 by 8 shape.
The middle ring.
The large ring.
A missile in flight: one pixel, in the shape's top left corner.
Flips missile_dot at the missile's position.
Flips the shape at $86/$87 at the missile's position (draw_shape).
After a war, in the letter window: each country's name and "has survived the war." or "Has been destroyed.", then waits for fire and closes the window.
